overview: Monte Alban was an important Zapotec capital in the Oaxaca Valley. Its history of urban planning, water management and carved inscriptions is one part of the much wider history of Zapotec societies.

items.text: Builders reshaped hillsides with terraces, dams and conduits. Water management and the creation of level spaces were integrated into urban development.
Temples and platforms framed a long ceremonial esplanade. Open spaces were as important to the layout as the buildings themselves.
Carved reliefs with hieroglyphic inscriptions survive alongside tombs and temples, giving evidence of visual art and record making.
The ceremonial center included a ball court. Its built spaces supported activities beyond the palaces and burial places of elites.
Monte Alban maintained relations with Teotihuacan. Those contacts connect Oaxaca's history to other contemporary Mesoamerican centers.
UNESCO dates Monte Alban's long florescence from about 500 BCE to 850 CE, followed by decline. This is the trajectory of a city, not an extinction date for Zapotec peoples.
